title: Lesson Plan — Real Numbers (Class 10 CBSE Mathematics)
subject: Mathematics
objectives: State and apply Euclid's division lemma; use the algorithm to find HCF.
State the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic; write prime factorisations.
Find HCF and LCM via prime factorisation; verify HCF × LCM = product.
Prove √2 (and similar) are irrational by contradiction.
Decide if a rational number has a terminating or non-terminating-repeating decimal.
prerequisites: Concepts of natural numbers, integers, rationals, irrationals from Class 9.
Multiplication and prime factorisation of small integers.
materials: A handout with sample 'terminate or not' fractions

activities.description: Hook: 'Find HCF(420, 130) WITHOUT listing factors.' Take guesses; show Euclid's algorithm in 3 lines.
Pair card sort: 6 pairs of integers; students find HCF using either algorithm (Euclid's) or prime factorisation. They must show working.

Three blocks: (i) Euclid's lemma + algorithm with worked example; (ii) Fundamental Theorem + HCF/LCM rules + identity HCF × LCM = product; (iii) irrational proof technique + decimal expansion theorem.
Worksheet practice: 5 items covering all topics.

homework: Find HCF and LCM of (i) 24 and 36; (ii) 18, 24, 30; (iii) 96 and 404. For each, verify HCF × LCM identity (where applicable).
Decide which of these have terminating decimals (without doing the division): 6/8, 7/12, 13/3125, 23/30, 17/40.
Write the proof that √5 is irrational. (Use the structure of the √2 proof.)
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as formative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on √3 proof using a structured rubric (assumption + algebra + contradiction).
references: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics textbook (jemh1dd), Chapter 1: Real Numbers.
